fixtures.label: pattern-skip-getBinding-walks-past-pattern
fixtures.input_source: const foo = 'outer'; function f({ foo }) { return foo; }
fixtures.//: Upstream-trace finding 2: getBinding walks past Pattern scopes when the encountered binding is NOT param/local. Inner reference-from-`return foo` resolves to the destructured `{ foo }` PARAM, NOT the outer `const foo`. This is the pattern-skip rule at scope/index.js:816. The §5.0a port must implement this walk. NB: when a param is a destructure, binding.path.node.type === 'ObjectPattern' (the whole pattern), NOT 'Identifier' — the Identifier inside the pattern is registered through getOuterBindingIdentifiers but the binding.path points at the pattern itself.

fixtures.label: var-in-for-loop-hoists-to-function-scope
fixtures.input_source: function f() { for (var x = 1; x < 10; x++) {} const y = x; }
fixtures.//: Upstream-trace finding 3: `var` in ForStatement init hoists to the enclosing function scope. The reference `const y = x;` AFTER the loop must resolve to the hoisted `var x`. ALSO triggers finding 4: `var` in loop body is auto-marked non-constant via Binding.isInitInLoop → reassign(). Reference count is 3 per Babel: x in test position (`x < 10`), x in `x++`, and x in `const y = x`. The `var x = 1` init position itself is the binding declaration, not a reference.

fixtures.//: Confirms Binding.constant is FALSE when reassign() fires from an AssignmentExpression. Same shape as `module-let-mutation-not-constant` but with `var` to verify the var-kind path is wired.
